orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Lok Pal Singh
orders.text:
WPSS No.2359 of 2019 
Hon’ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
 
 Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
 Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the 
respondents. 
 Learned counsel for the petitioner presses 
for interim order in the matter on the ground 
that in all the other connected writ petitions, 
there is interim order of the Court directing the 
respondents to pay minimum of pay scale to the 
petitioners. He submits that the controversy 
involved in these writ petitions is similar and 
prayed to grant similar interim order in his case 
also. 
 Though, the interim relief application filed 
by the petitioner was dismissed by this Court, 
vide order dated 29.11.2019, but as similarly 
situated persons have been granted minimum 
of pay scale by the interim orders of this Court 
passed in connected writ petitions, petitioner 
deserves similar relief. 
 Thereafter, as an interim measure, it is 
directed that the respondents shall pay 
minimum of pay scale to the petitioner. 
 Pleadings have been exchanged. 
 List for final disposal in the first week of 
January 2021, along with connected matter. 
 
 
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.) 
 25.11.2020
Rajni

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 2359 of 2019
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate along with 
Mr. Priyanshu Gairola, Advocate, for the 
petitioner.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate, for the 
respondents.
All the facts, which have been sought 
to be pressed by the respondents, by virtue of 
the Recall Application No. 15681/2021, were 
the facts, which were available on record at the 
time when the coordinate Bench of this Court 
had passed an interim order of payment of 
minimum wages to the petitioner on 
25.11.2020. 
It is not reflected that the applicant to 
the Recall Application had argued these 
grounds before the coordinate Bench of this 
Court. Hence, I do not find any reason to recall 
the interim order, as sought for by the Recall 
Application. 
Consequently, the Recall Application 
lacks merits and the same is hereby dismissed.
List this writ petition in the week 
commencing 12.04.2021 for final hearing.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 22.03.2021 Mahinder/

Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate, for the 
petitioners in connected matters. 
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate, for the 
respondent(s).
The petitioners of this bunch of writ 
petitions are claiming their respective 
regularisation under the Regularisation Rules of 
2013, the effect of which, has already been kept 
in abeyance in the proceedings which are sub 
judice before the Division Bench. The Division 
Bench is yet to decide the matter, about the 
validity of the Regularisation Rules of 2013.
In that eventuality, where by a judicial 
order the Regularisation Rules have been kept 
in abeyance, this bunch of writ petitions, where 
the respective petitioners have claimed their 
regularisation, cannot be considered till the 
matter is decided by the Division Bench. 
Hence, put up this bunch of writ 
petitions, as soon as the Division Bench decides 
the matter on its own merit, pertaining to 
validity of the Regularisation Rules of 2013.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 15.06.2022 Mahinder/
